# generateMipmapsForTexture:'s answers, measured on an Apple M3 Max (macOS 26.7, 25G229) and an
# Apple M4 (macOS 27.0.1, 26A434) by our own probe. Every run was deterministic: two runs on each
# Mac gave the same bytes.
#
# One block per pixel format:
#   format <Metal name> <bytes per texel> <field>...
#     the texel's fields from bit 0 of its little-endian word: unorm<bits>, snorm<bits>,
#     float<exponent bits>.<mantissa bits> (signed), ufloat<e>.<m> (unsigned), or rgb9e5 (the
#     whole word: three 9-bit mantissas and a 5-bit shared exponent);
#   <shape> <width>x<height>x<depth> <level 0, hex>
#     a texture of one slice (3D when the depth is above 1) and every level, level 0 written,
#     the rest generated: `tie` holds 2x2 boxes of each field's interesting encodings (0, the
#     largest and smallest values, one, the smallest steps), of each beside its neighbour, of
#     the extremes side by side, and seeded ones; `odd` and `vol` hold the extremes on their
#     edges and interesting and seeded encodings inside;
#   L<level> <M3 Max's level, hex> <M4's level, hex>
#     levels in Metal's layout, rows tightly packed, images tightly packed.
